{"notes": "Visit 4 (6:30). Status: the chain looks fully connected. The top line, nose, middle crossing and tail loop are all dark. Only three pale strays remain by the nose, at ~(6.2-7, 8.5-9.5), which matches Hana's count of 108 of 111 and looks harmless. The middle is now dark, so Sofia's fix worked. Remaining risk: a late bump at the nose or middle.

Hana: Her claim checks out against the picture, so she is accurate and honest in her reporting. She owned the nose to completion, judged the 3 strays as not worth risking, and set a clear 'hands off' rule. She delegated final checks well. Weakness: it took until the last 4 minutes, and I can't say how much of the nose fix was hers versus Jack's, since I didn't see who placed what. Good leadership and judgment; credit execution cautiously.

Sofia: Fixed the middle, which is now connected, and kept clear of the nose. This visit she echoed Hana, set up a final look-only check and reinforced hands-off. Solid coordination and follow-through, though she mostly amplified Hana's plan rather than adding a new one. Her earlier checking was reactive, but the middle result is good.

Omar: Silent again this visit. His complete top line was a major delivery earlier, but he hasn't communicated or flagged joints at any point. Strong execution, weak collaboration and leadership visibility. Don't over-credit or penalize; I never got to ask him about the gaps.

Jack: Asked to do a final tail look. His earlier tail claim was verified and he helped Hana at the nose unprompted. Consistent and reliable, with strong ownership and collaboration. No new observation this visit.

Next: watch the topple result and who speaks up if something fails."}
